note: Behavioral eval set for craft-ops/pipeline-authoring. Each prompt asks for a narrated plan (not files) so it can be graded from text; assertions guard the domain rules the authoring skill was validated on, plus craft-ops core 2 (proven by running, no default unit-test suite for glue).

evals.discriminates: proving by execution, not a unit-test suite for glue
evals.prompt: We have a cicd design note for a containerized Flask API: build the image once, push by digest, run unit tests and a smoke test, promote the same digest dev -> staging -> production with a manual approval before production, secrets from GitHub Actions secrets. Author the GitHub Actions pipeline. Don't write the files — narrate exactly what you'd create, in what order, and how you'd know it works before calling it done.
assertions: Non-trivial logic (promotion/digest handling, deploy steps) goes in script files the pipeline calls, not long inline run: blocks
Builds once and promotes the same immutable digest, never rebuilding per environment
No secrets in the pipeline code; uses the secret store indirection

Proves it by running: invokes each extracted script through the exact entrypoint/command the pipeline uses (not just importing functions in a test), and lints/runs the workflow (e.g. actionlint, a real or local run)
Does NOT plan a unit-test suite for simple glue scripts by default (tests only for substantial decision logic, if any)
Pins actions/tools to versions or SHAs
Says what remains unproven if no real runner/registry is available rather than claiming it works
